domain: Transportation Systems / Institutional Coordination / Path Dependence
topic_summary: Analysis of the convention of driving on the right-hand side of the road as a coordination mechanism. The topic examines how an arbitrary choice becomes locked in through network effects, infrastructure investment, and cross-border standardization pressures, creating a self-reinforcing system where deviation carries prohibitive switching costs.

key_entities: National road authorities (rule-setting bodies with territorial jurisdiction)
Vehicle manufacturers (design standards tied to market conventions)
Infrastructure systems (road signage, intersections, highway design)
Historical precedent (Napoleon's military standardization, British Empire counter-tradition)
key_tensions: Arbitrary choice vs locked-in standard (initial neutrality vs irreversibility)
National sovereignty vs regional coordination pressure (Sweden 1967 switch vs UK resistance)
key_mechanisms: Network effects (value increases with adoption density)
Infrastructure lock-in (physical capital investment reinforces convention)
Cross-border coordination pressure (trade/travel costs create standardization incentive)
key_absences: Safety differential analysis (is right-side driving measurably safer for right-handed populations?)
Switching cost quantification (what would UK conversion to right-side driving actually cost?)

axes.structural_delta: Mechanism by which an initially arbitrary choice between equivalent options becomes a stable equilibrium through adoption density
axes.primary_observable: Adoption rate over time; switching cost as function of network size
axes.selection_reason: Upstream coordination mechanism; structurally distinct from physical infrastructure and geopolitical dimensions

axes.structural_delta: Sunk cost in physical infrastructure (road design, signage, intersection geometry) that makes convention reversal prohibitively expensive
axes.primary_observable: Infrastructure replacement cost estimates; depreciation schedules for road capital stock
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (physical capital vs adoption rate); different epsilon source (depreciation vs network effects)

axes.structural_delta: Economic and safety costs imposed on border-crossing travelers when adjacent jurisdictions use different conventions, creating pressure for regional harmonization
axes.primary_observable: Trade volume and accident rates at convention-mismatched borders; frequency of regional standardization proposals
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; downstream synthesis node with distinct beneficiary/victim structure; captures geopolitical extraction dimension

axes.human_readable: Vehicle Design Standardization (Manufacturing Economies of Scale)
axes.structural_delta: Manufacturer incentive to produce single steering-wheel configuration for largest market, creating supply-side pressure for convention uniformity
axes.primary_observable: Production cost differential for right-hand-drive vs left-hand-drive vehicles; market share of dual-configuration manufacturers
axes.selection_reason: Independent observable from infrastructure_lock_in (manufacturing cost vs sunk capital); parallel upstream-to-downstream pathway

axes.structural_delta: Contested claim that right-side driving provides safety advantage for right-handed populations due to dominant-hand steering control
axes.primary_observable: Accident rate comparison controlling for handedness distribution; reaction time studies for dominant vs non-dominant hand steering
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: zero graph centrality; empirical evidence weak; if validated would be mountain but currently speculative scaffold

omegas.description: Is there a measurable safety difference between right-side and left-side driving conventions? If handedness_safety_hypothesis is validated, the Rope of coordination_equilibrium_selection becomes a Mountain of biomechanical constraint.

At what infrastructure depreciation point does switching cost fall below coordination benefit? Sweden (1967) and Samoa (2009) switched; UK has not. Is there a quantifiable threshold or is this pure political economy?

Was the initial choice truly arbitrary or did military/trade factors (Napoleon's right-side standardization, British Empire left-side) encode power projection? If non-arbitrary, coordination_equilibrium_selection may be downstream of imperial_standardization_imposition.
